description:
We are looking for a seasoned Principal Product Manager to define and deliver task automation for lending, built on a shared workflow platform. It helps financial institutions automate the repetitive, rules-driven tasks that slow a loan down, combining deterministic business logic with AI-driven steps so more loans move straight through with less manual effort.

This role sits at the intersection of lending operations, workflow technology, and applied AI. You will turn the way lenders actually work (the tasks, documents, data, and decisions at each stage of a loan) into configurable, reusable automation that works across multiple products.

This is one of the company's most strategic initiatives, with direct visibility to executive leadership. You will be the first dedicated product leader on a new team, shaping the shared framework, the initial scope alongside product teams, and the roadmap from the ground up.

You have shipped workflow, automation, or platform products to external customers, not just internal tools or prototypes, and you are comfortable making decisions in a space where the use cases are still being proven.

Key Responsibilities:

Product Strategy and Roadmap

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for the shared task automation framework and workflow platform that multiple lending products build on.

  • Partner with executive leadership to align automation priorities with company-wide product vision and revenue goals.

  • Work with product teams to decide which customer segments to serve first and how to package automation for them, from ready-made workflows to fully configurable rules, based on customer evidence.

  • Define what belongs in the shared platform and what belongs in each product, and keep that boundary clear for the teams building on it.

  • Build business cases that quantify customer value (hours and dollars saved) and support investment, packaging, and pricing decisions.

  • Own the commercial model for task automation: how it is packaged, priced, and sold, with pricing and sales partners.

  • Evaluate build, buy, and partner options for core components, including open-source and cloud services, and make the tradeoffs visible.

  • Coach other product managers and raise the standard for how AI and automation products are defined, evaluated, and measured.

Discovery and Customer Engagement

  • Conduct deep discovery with lending operations teams, loan processors, compliance officers, and technology buyers to understand how workflows differ across institutions and where manual work concentrates.

  • Test whether customers will adopt configurable automation, how much control they need, and which customer segments want ready-made workflows versus hands-on configuration, using design partners and early-access customers.

  • Lead rapid prototyping, including with AI tools, to test workflow concepts with design partners before committing to a build.

  • Synthesize qualitative research, product usage data, and competitive intelligence into clear opportunities.

Cross-Functional Delivery

  • Drive execution with engineering, architecture, and design teams across several product lines using agile practices.

  • Translate platform needs into clear epics, requirements, and acceptance criteria, including workflow definition, triggers, human review steps, rules configuration, and audit trails.

  • Partner with product teams to integrate the platform into their products and sequence the work.

  • Define the events, APIs, and third-party integrations each product needs to expose so workflows can trigger on any event and take any action a user can take.

  • Define where AI belongs, both as steps inside a mostly deterministic workflow and as help for customers configuring workflows, including human-in-the-loop review, exception handling, and escalation.

  • Coordinate with compliance, legal, and information security so automated actions meet regulatory expectations (FCRA, ECOA, fair lending, model risk management, auditability).

  • Own launch readiness: go-to-market coordination, documentation, training, and customer communication.

Measurement and Iteration

  • Define and track outcomes such as straight-through processing rate, automation rate, exception volume, cycle time, cost per loan, and adoption.

  • Build feedback loops that surface failures and edge cases quickly and turn them into iteration cycles.

  • Communicate performance transparently to leadership and stakeholders.

Qualifications:

Product Management

  • 8+ years of product management experience in an enterprise B2B SaaS environment, including 3+ years owning a workflow, orchestration, rules or decisioning, low-code, or process automation product.

  • Experience building platform or shared-capability products that other product teams build on, including APIs, integration contracts, and internal customers.

  • Proven ability to set direction where use cases are not yet proven and much of the dependent work sits on other teams' roadmaps: form a point of view, test it with customer evidence, resolve competing views from deep domain experts, and bring senior engineering and business leaders along.

  • Experience defining packaging and pricing for enterprise software, ideally platform or workflow products.

  • Experience conducting customer and user research and translating insights into product strategy.

  • Mastery of agile methodologies. Strong problem-solving, storytelling, and presentation skills.

  • Excellent collaboration skills within and across teams.

Automation and AI Experience

  • Demonstrated track record of taking workflow or automation features from concept to production for external customers, not internal tooling or prototypes.

  • Working knowledge of how AI fits into automation, including LLMs and agentic patterns, evaluations, human-in-the-loop design, and quality and accuracy metrics.

  • Familiarity with workflow engines, event-driven architectures, and integration approaches, enough to work credibly with senior engineers on tradeoffs.

  • Familiarity with responsible AI principles, explainability, and auditability in regulated environments.

Background and Education

  • Bachelor's degree required; MBA preferred. Computer science background (education or other demonstrated proficiency) preferred.

  • Experience with loan origination systems or lender operations (rules, conditions, tasks, service ordering) is strongly preferred.
